chunks: He said: 'Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them; and I am among the witnesses to that.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the Lord of the heavens and earth according to this verse?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Anbiya, this verse underscores the monotheistic argument against idolatry by identifying Allah as the sole Creator (Al-Fattar) of the cosmos, a theme central to the prophetic mission. Shia exegetes often highlight the phrase 'wa ana 'ala dhalika mina ash-shahidin' as affirming the prophet's role as a divine witness, linking the act of creation to the eventual establishment of divine authority through the Ahl al-Bayt.
